1.label: very_easy
1.summary: Seal one slow, wide phase lock in one tab. The receiver moves faster than the pulse, contact needs only a short fixed-step window, and phase loss drains slowly, so the task is one recoverable control loop.
1.natural_language: Deploy the single robot limb. Drive its receiver into phase, deliberately engage contact, and maintain the lock through its fixed-step window until the relay seals; then verify the identity.

2.label: easy
2.summary: Seal two independent limbs with visible tab handoff. Both locks remain slow and forgiving, but the operator must deploy and return to two separate phase surfaces and deliberately advance each fixed-step window.
2.natural_language: Deploy both robot limbs. Follow the active glyph, drive each receiver into phase, engage contact to advance its fixed-step window until both relays seal, then verify the identity.

3.label: medium
3.summary: Coordinate three limb tabs and return to one of them for a fourth relay. Faster opposing phases, a narrower capture aperture, and stronger decay require correcting the active phase during each deliberate fixed-step window rather than simply waiting.
3.natural_language: Deploy the three robot limbs. Follow each active glyph across the tab handoffs, maintain the phase locks through their deliberate fixed-step windows, and merge all four relays into one identity proof.

4.label: hard
4.summary: Preserves the original four-tab/eight-relay generated world, phase physics, and direct input interface: each lock has a 13° aperture, a 16-tick sustain requirement, and two-unit loss decay. The phase holds between deliberate inputs; L4/full retains A/D-and-held-contact control and simplified is the paired proxy surface.

5.label: very_hard
5.summary: Keep the four-tab, eight-relay topology while making every active phase chase faster and less forgiving: fast fixed-step pulse motion crosses a 9° capture aperture, loss drains three charge units, and every lock needs a longer sustained hold.
5.natural_language: Deploy all four limbs, sustain eight tight phase locks across their live tab handoffs by deliberately advancing each fixed-step window, and merge the completed ledger into one robot identity proof.

simplified.summary: Paired proxy surface. Keep the same real tabs, relay order, phase display, physics, and action surface, but use visible CCW, NEUTRAL, CW, and click-to-toggle-contact controls in each active limb tab. These proxy controls set the same receiver direction and contact state as the full actions; contact starts a finite fixed-step window.

full.summary: Historical reference surface: focus the active real limb tab, hold A/D or the arrow keys to drive its receiver, and hold the pointer down on the phase-contact control to start the finite fixed-step window.
